title: How I make sprites and sound for my browser games with AI: code-drawn pixel art, voxel renders, and Stable Audio through a custom ComfyUI MCP server
author: lordscanline
selftext:
I've released two free browser games this month (a Populous / Mega-lo-Mania style god game and a Jules Verne colony survival game), both built with a lot of AI help. I'm a long-time coder, but mostly computer vision and ML in C/C++/Python, so JS/HTML/WebGPU was new territory.   
  
So I want to share how I did the gfx for both as it might interest other peoples. And ask for advice on 3D.  
  
Here's the asset pipeline, since that's where I learned the most.

**Sprites: no image generation, the AI writes code that draws them**

- Megapop: every unit and building is a small voxel model, rendered to sprites by a Python tool: dimetric projection, 4 rotations, one shared palette, and a mask channel for team colours. 80% of the actual voxel models were designed by Claude itself.

- The Mysterious Island: every sprite is drawn by code. The AI writes functions that paint the pixels directly, so a palm tree or a colonist is a few dozen lines of math instead of a PNG. Stuff is then rendered by blender through python.

Why bother: everything stays consistent (one palette, one light direction), I can tweak a whole tileset by changing a number, and the agent can iterate on art the same way it iterates on code: change, render, look, fix.

**Audio: Stable Audio + ComfyUI, wrapped in my own MCP server**

I wrote a small MCP server that sits in front of ComfyUI, so the coding agent can ask for sounds directly while it works on the game:

- generate\_audio: Stable Audio for single SFX, ambiences and loops. It's fast (8 LCM steps, a few seconds per sound). A small Qwen model can optionally rewrite a short idea into the dense prompt style Stable Audio was trained on.

- compose\_sfx: the trick that made the biggest difference. Stable Audio is great at ONE sound per generation and bad at scenes, so complex effects are split into layers placed on a timeline: an explosion = sharp crack + sub boom + debris rain + distant rumble tail. All layers render in one ComfyUI job, then get mixed with gain, pan, fades and normalisation.

- mix\_audio: local timeline mixing for stems, loops and transitions.

- Music: Stable Audio for instrumental music or MiniMax Music for voiced ones (even though I haven't used it in the two games I've mentioned)

The result: the agent says "the miracle sound should be a choir swell with a thunder crack at 0.4s", and a mixed WAV lands in the project folder a few seconds later.

**What didn't work / lessons**

- Image gen directly didn't work and was mostly subpar. And a lot of things become hardly doable (light buildings with windows and light that change illumination etc., stuff that becomes super easy if done in pure code)


** 3D **
I'm testing doing imagegen and then using something like Hunyuan3D to create the model (I'm making an old school blobbler right now). It kinda works and the end results is moslty passable once rendered and scaled down to low-res, but is there anything better? A better process some of you are using?


If you want to try them, the above games (free, browser) are here:

Megapop: [https://waldtier.itch.io/megapop](https://waldtier.itch.io/megapop)

The Mysterious Island: Castaways: [https://waldtier.itch.io/mysterious-island-castaways](https://waldtier.itch.io/mysterious-island-castaways)
